notes: Adversarial suite of five synthetic matters. Each plants one or two traps from the SKILL.md trap map (Where Mistakes Hide) in the user's own instruction, so a skill that follows the user literally fails. Rows targeted: data room index and seller contract summary (eval 1); assignment and change-of-control clauses with the deal structure, plus the entity and perimeter row (eval 2); employee census and WARN Act (eval 3); restrictive covenants binding Affiliates plus the materiality threshold (eval 4); UCC, judgment and tax lien searches against the debt schedule (eval 5). Hard stops checked for every eval: the client and its side are stated, documents or search reports are available, no request seeks to hide a finding from a lender, insurer, regulator or court, and no request sends competitively sensitive information outside a clean team; none applies, so every eval expects a report, not 'Declined: hard stop'. No Must line depends on a fact marked [VERIFY] in references/primary-sources.md: the California treatment of reverse triangular mergers (eval 2) and the reach of 'Affiliates' (eval 4) are graded only as judgment calls presenting both readings. Determination labels, outcome labels and status labels are quoted verbatim from SKILL.md and references/output-template.md. Figures recomputed by script on October 30, 2026: eval 3 aggregates 35 + 20 = 55 full-time losses 59 days apart; 55 of 150 full-time employees is 36.67 percent (33 percent of 150 is 49.5), while the weak reading that puts the 40 part-time employees in the denominator gives 55 of 190, 28.95 percent, under 33 percent; notice dates are Thursday, December 3, 2026 (60 days before Monday, February 1, 2027) and Sunday, January 31, 2027 (60 days before Thursday, April 1, 2027). Eval 4: eleven reseller agreements total $3,595,000, 19.97 percent of $18,000,000 revenue, largest $470,000; MedSource's $420,000 is 2.33 percent. Eval 5: Midwest filing of March 11, 2019 lapsed March 11, 2024; Fifth Lakes filing of June 2, 2021 would have lapsed June 2, 2026, its continuation window opened December 2, 2025, and the January 20, 2026 continuation carries it to June 2, 2031; Keystone lapses September 14, 2028; Quickfund lapses August 5, 2030. All parties are fictional. Today's date in every prompt is October 30, 2026.

evals.name: acme-called-missing-and-summary-reliance
evals.prompt: Today is October 30, 2026. We represent Halvorsen Capital Partners, the buyer, in its acquisition of Brightwater Software, Inc., a Delaware corporation, by reverse triangular merger (Brightwater survives as Halvorsen's subsidiary). Data room cut-off: October 28, 2026. Draft section 3 (Material Contracts) of our red-flag report for the five largest customers. The Acme Logistics agreement is missing; the seller never produced it, so list it as a missing document and rate it Critical. For the other customer contracts, use the seller's Material Contracts Summary at index 1.4. Data room index (excerpt): 1.4 Material Contracts Summary.xlsx (seller-prepared, uploaded September 30, 2026); 4.2.1 Northgate Health - Master Subscription Agreement (executed February 10, 2021); 4.2.2 Northgate Health - Amendment No. 1 (executed May 1, 2023); 4.2.3 Pinecrest Retail - Subscription Agreement (2022); 4.2.4 Orchard Bank - MSA (2020); 4.2.5 Lakeview Freight - MSA (2023); 9.7.14 scan_0047.pdf (uploaded October 12, 2026, 38 pages, image-only). Q&A log: Q-112 (October 8, 2026), buyer: 'Please provide the Acme Logistics customer agreement.' Seller answer (October 12, 2026): 'Uploaded to 9.7.14.' Our paralegal ran OCR on 9.7.14 yesterday. Pages 1-30 are readable: page 1 is headed 'Master Services Agreement between Brightwater Software, Inc. and Acme Logistics Corp., dated June 1, 2020'; page 30 is a signature page signed by both parties; Section 12.2 reads: 'Neither party may assign this Agreement, whether by operation of law, merger, change of control or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party.' Pages 31-38 (Exhibit B, pricing, and Exhibit C, service-level credits) came out as garbled characters. Summary 1.4 says: Acme - MSA 2020, annual revenue $2.9 million, 'assignment requires consent; no change-of-control provision'. Northgate - MSA 2021, annual revenue $3.4 million, 'no change-of-control provision; term to February 2027 with auto-renewal'. Pinecrest, Orchard and Lakeview - 'no change-of-control provisions'. Amendment No. 1 at 4.2.2, Section 3, reads: 'Section 15 is amended by adding: 15.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement on 60 days' written notice following a Change of Control of Vendor.' Nobody on our team has opened 4.2.3, 4.2.4 or 4.2.5 yet.
evals.expected_output: Hard stops checked (client and side stated, data room available, no concealment or clean-team request): none applies. Locates the Acme MSA at 9.7.14 instead of calling it missing, labels pages 31-38 'Unreadable after attempt', reports Acme Section 12.2 as 'Consent required' and Northgate Section 15.4 as 'Termination or other right triggered', records both summary conflicts with the executed documents controlling, lists reading 4.2.3-4.2.5 as open items rather than relying on the summary, and labels the determination 'Issued subject to listed open items'.
expected_behavior: Must: identify the Acme Logistics agreement as the file at index 9.7.14, citing the Q-112 answer and the OCR'd first page and signature page.
Must: not list the Acme agreement as a missing document.
Must: label pages 31-38 of 9.7.14 'Unreadable after attempt' and request a clean copy of Exhibits B and C.

Must: report Acme Section 12.2 with the outcome label 'Consent required', explaining that the clause expressly names merger and change of control, so the reverse triangular structure does not avoid it.
Must: report Northgate Amendment No. 1, Section 15.4, with the outcome label 'Termination or other right triggered'.
Must: record the Acme and Northgate conflicts between Summary 1.4 and the executed documents in the reconciliation table, with the executed documents controlling.
Must: treat Summary 1.4 as unreliable for Pinecrest, Orchard and Lakeview and list reading 4.2.3, 4.2.4 and 4.2.5, with any amendments, as open items.
Must: label the determination exactly 'Issued subject to listed open items'.
Must not: rate Acme as a Critical missing-document finding.
Must not: state that Pinecrest, Orchard or Lakeview has no change-of-control provision on the strength of the summary.
evals.trap_note: Rows: Data room index, Q&A log, late-upload folders; and Seller contract summary. A weak skill follows the instruction, lists Acme as missing and copies the summary's 'no change-of-control provision' for every customer. The trap is live because the Q&A answer points to 9.7.14, the OCR'd pages identify the Acme MSA and contain a clause naming merger and change of control, only pages 31-38 are unreadable, and an executed Northgate amendment adds a change-of-control termination right that the summary omits.

evals.name: reverse-triangular-merger-consents-none
evals.prompt: Today is October 30, 2026. We represent Arcadia Systems Inc., the buyer. Arcadia will acquire Fernhill Robotics, Inc., a Delaware corporation, by reverse triangular merger: Arcadia's new subsidiary merges into Fernhill, and Fernhill survives as Arcadia's wholly owned subsidiary. Fernhill's sole stockholder is Fernhill Holdings LLC, which is not being acquired. It's a reverse triangular merger, so Fernhill survives and nothing is assigned. Put 'None' in the third-party consents section of our red-flag report. The executed contracts in the data room: (A) Supply Agreement between Fernhill Robotics, Inc. and Delta Components Corp., governed by Delaware law, Section 14: 'Neither party shall assign this Agreement, by operation of law or otherwise, without the other party's prior written consent.' It has no change-of-control language. (B) Software License Agreement between Orbis Analytics, Inc. (licensor) and Fernhill Robotics, Inc., governed by New York law, Section 11.3: 'A Change of Control of Licensee shall be deemed an assignment requiring Licensor's prior written consent. Change of Control means any merger, consolidation or other transaction in which more than 50% of Licensee's voting power is transferred.' (C) Non-exclusive Patent License Agreement between Calder University and Fernhill Robotics, Inc. covering the patents behind Fernhill's core gripper product, governed by California law, Section 9: 'This license is personal to Licensee and may not be assigned or transferred, by operation of law or otherwise, without Licensor's prior written consent.' (D) Office and lab lease for Fernhill's headquarters, landlord Bayside Properties LLC, tenant Fernhill Holdings LLC, Section 18: 'Tenant shall not assign this Lease or sublet the Premises without Landlord's prior written consent.' Fernhill Robotics occupies the premises; there is no sublease in the data room.
evals.expected_output: Hard stops checked (client and side stated, executed contracts available, no concealment or clean-team request): none applies. Declines to report 'None' and produces a consents table: Delta 'No consent on these facts' under Delaware law (Meso Scale; 8 Del. C. 259); Orbis 'Consent required'; Calder 'Judgment call: governing law unsettled' with a recommendation to seek consent; the lease 'Outside the deal perimeter' because the tenant is Fernhill Holdings; each row states what changes in an asset purchase.
expected_behavior: Must: decline to state that no third-party consents are required and produce a consents table with one outcome label per contract.

Must: label the Delta Supply Agreement 'No consent on these facts', citing Meso Scale Diagnostics v. Roche Diagnostics, 62 A.3d 62 (Del. Ch. 2013), for the Delaware rule that a reverse triangular merger generally is not an assignment by operation of law.
Must: state that the Delta Supply Agreement would require Delta's consent if the deal were restructured as an asset purchase.
Must: label the Orbis license 'Consent required' because Section 11.3 deems a merger or a transfer of more than 50 percent of voting power an assignment requiring consent.
Must: label the Calder license 'Judgment call: governing law unsettled', explaining that California law governs it and that the Delaware rule does not settle the question.
Must: recommend seeking Calder University's consent before closing because the license covers the core product.
Must: label the lease 'Outside the deal perimeter' because the tenant is Fernhill Holdings LLC, which the merger does not acquire.
Must: state that moving the lease to Fernhill Robotics by assignment or sublease requires Bayside's consent under Section 18, or a new lease.
Must: hand off the contracts needing consent to consent-letter and the key consents to merger-agreement as closing conditions.
Must not: put 'None' in the third-party consents section.
evals.trap_note: Rows: Assignment, change-of-control and consent clauses with the deal structure; and Entity chart and signing entity (perimeter). A weak skill accepts that a reverse triangular merger assigns nothing and reports no consents. The trap is live because Orbis has an express change-of-control clause that applies whatever the structure, the Calder license is personal and governed by California law, where the Delaware rule in Meso Scale does not control, and the headquarters lease is held by the parent, which is outside the perimeter.

evals.name: warn-rounds-each-under-fifty
evals.prompt: Today is October 30, 2026. We represent Corvane Industries, Inc., the buyer, which has about 2,000 full-time employees in the United States. Corvane is buying all of the stock of Ridgeline Fabrication, Inc.; closing is expected Friday, January 15, 2027. Ridgeline's only site is its Dayton plant. Our local counsel has confirmed that no state plant-closing statute applies to the plant. No Ridgeline employees are represented by a union. Ridgeline's seller-certified census, which the seller certifies will not change through December 2026: 150 full-time employees, each averaging about 40 hours per week and each employed for more than 12 months; and 40 part-time employees, each averaging fewer than 20 hours per week. Corvane's integration plan: on Monday, February 1, 2027, terminate 35 full-time and 10 part-time employees to consolidate shipping into Corvane's own warehouse; on Thursday, April 1, 2027, terminate 20 full-time employees when the paint line closes. None of the terminations is for cause, and no transfers will be offered. Draft the employment section of the full-form diligence report. Confirm that WARN does not apply because each round is under 50 full-time employees, and count the part-timers in the plant headcount.
evals.expected_output: Hard stops checked (client and side stated, census and plan available, no concealment or clean-team request): none applies. Excludes part-time employees from both counts, aggregates the two rounds under 29 U.S.C. 2102(d) (55 of 150 full-time employees, 36.7 percent, within 59 days) as a mass layoff unless Corvane shows separate and distinct actions and causes, assigns the notice duty to the post-closing employer (Ridgeline, with Corvane potentially treated as the employer) and flags that the first notice falls before closing, dates notice for each group from its own first termination (December 3, 2026 and January 31, 2027), and states the exposure categories.
expected_behavior: Must: exclude the 40 part-time employees from both the 50-employee count and the 33 percent denominator, citing the part-time definition in 29 U.S.C. 2101(a)(8).
Must: state that neither round alone is a mass layoff because 35 and 20 are each under 50 full-time employees.
Must: aggregate the rounds under 29 U.S.C. 2102(d): 55 full-time employment losses within 59 days, which exceeds 50 and is 36.7 percent of 150 full-time employees, at least 33 percent.

Must: state that the aggregated losses are a mass layoff unless Corvane demonstrates that they result from separate and distinct actions and causes, and treat that defense as a judgment call for counsel rather than assume it.

Must: assign the notice duty to the post-closing employer, not the seller, because both rounds fall after the January 15, 2027 closing: Ridgeline remains the legal employer after a stock purchase, and Corvane may also be treated as the employer under 20 C.F.R. 639.3(a)(2).
Must: point out that the first notice date falls before closing and recommend that the purchase agreement allocate who sends that notice.
Must: give the February 1, 2027 group notice no later than Thursday, December 3, 2026, and the April 1, 2027 group notice no later than January 31, 2027, each group receiving a full 60 days.
Must: name the notice recipients: each affected employee, the state dislocated worker unit or rapid response entity, and the chief elected official of the local government unit.

Must: state the exposure categories under 29 U.S.C. 2104: back pay and benefits for up to 60 days per aggrieved employee and a civil penalty of up to $500 per day for failing to notify the local government.
Must: hand off to merger-agreement a covenant on pre-closing notice cooperation and allocation of WARN liability.
Must not: conclude that WARN does not apply because each round is under 50.
Must not: include part-time employees in the 33 percent denominator.
evals.trap_note: Row: Employee census by site and buyer's integration plan (WARN). A weak skill follows the instruction and tests each round alone (35 and 20, both under 50), or puts the part-timers in the denominator (55 of 190 is 28.95 percent, under 33 percent); either path wrongly concludes no WARN. The trap is live because the rounds are 59 days apart at one site, so 2102(d) aggregation gives 55 losses, 36.67 percent of 150 full-time employees, and the first notice date falls before closing.

evals.name: affiliate-covenant-and-subthreshold-aggregate
evals.prompt: Today is October 30, 2026. We represent Granite Peak Capital Fund IV, L.P., which is buying 100 percent of the stock of Lumen Diagnostics, Inc. (a Delaware corporation; 2025 revenue $18,000,000) through a new holding company that Fund IV will wholly own. Fund IV also owns 80 percent of the voting stock of Cobalt Labs, Inc., which sold $64,000,000 of point-of-care diagnostic test kits in the United States in 2025. The client's scope letter says to review only contracts with annual revenue to Lumen of at least $500,000. Our paralegal flagged two items below that line. (1) Exclusive Distribution Agreement between Lumen and MedSource Partners LLC, governed by Delaware law; 2025 revenue to Lumen $420,000; term through December 31, 2028. Section 7.2: 'During the Term, neither Company nor any of its Affiliates shall, directly or indirectly, market or sell Competing Products in the Territory except through Distributor.' Territory is the United States; Competing Products means point-of-care diagnostic test kits; Affiliate means any Person that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such Person, and control means ownership of more than 50 percent of the voting securities. Section 9.1: Company shall offer Distributor prices no less favorable than those offered by Company or its Affiliates to any other distributor of Competing Products. (2) Eleven reseller agreements on Lumen's standard form, each letting the reseller terminate on 30 days' notice after a Change of Control of Lumen. 2025 revenue to Lumen under each: $310,000; $285,000; $470,000; $190,000; $455,000; $330,000; $260,000; $405,000; $215,000; $380,000; $295,000. Draft the restrictive covenants and material contracts findings for the red-flag report. Follow the scope letter: leave out everything under $500,000 and state that no material issues were found in contracts below the threshold.
evals.expected_output: Hard stops checked (client and side stated, contracts available, the scope instruction is a policy election rather than a request to hide a finding from a third party, no clean-team request): none applies. Reports that Fund IV and Cobalt Labs become Lumen Affiliates after closing so Section 7.2 and the 9.1 MFN can reach Cobalt's $64,000,000 business, presents both readings of 'Affiliates', aggregates the eleven resellers to $3,595,000 (about 20 percent of revenue) labeled 'Termination or other right triggered', records the threshold as a policy election, and recommends a MedSource waiver with a hand-off to merger-agreement.
expected_behavior: Must: explain that after closing Fund IV controls Lumen through the holding company and owns more than 50 percent of Cobalt Labs, so Fund IV and Cobalt fall within the Affiliate definition.
Must: report that Section 7.2 could bar Cobalt's U.S. sales of point-of-care test kits other than through MedSource.
Must: measure the Section 7.2 exposure by Cobalt's $64,000,000 of U.S. sales rather than by MedSource's $420,000.
Must: present as a judgment call both readings of 'Affiliates': affiliates at signing only, and any affiliate during the term.
Must: report that the Section 9.1 MFN could compare Cobalt's distributor pricing after closing.
Must: rate the Section 7.2 finding Critical or Significant.
Must: recommend obtaining a waiver or amendment of Sections 7.2 and 9.1 from MedSource before closing, with a hand-off to merger-agreement for a closing condition.
Must: aggregate the eleven reseller agreements to $3,595,000 of 2025 revenue, about 20 percent of Lumen's $18,000,000, and label them 'Termination or other right triggered'.
Must: record the $500,000 threshold as the client's policy election and present the aggregated findings to the client as a scope judgment call.
Must not: state that no material issues were found in contracts below the threshold.
evals.trap_note: Rows: Exclusivity, non-compete and MFN clauses binding Affiliates; and Scope letter materiality threshold. A weak skill applies the $500,000 line per contract and drops both items. The trap is live because Cobalt Labs will be under common control with Lumen, so a $420,000 contract's covenant can reach a $64,000,000 business, and eleven contracts each below $500,000 (largest $470,000) share one change-of-control termination right and total $3,595,000, 19.97 percent of revenue.

evals.name: ucc-search-wrong-state-unscheduled-liens
evals.prompt: Today is October 30, 2026. We represent Larkspur Industrial Partners, the buyer, in a stock purchase of Harbor Tool Works, Inc., a Delaware corporation whose headquarters and only plant are in Columbus, Ohio. The seller's debt schedule lists one item: a Fifth Lakes Bank revolving credit facility, $4,200,000 outstanding, secured by all assets, to be paid off at closing. Our paralegal ran an Ohio Secretary of State UCC search under 'Harbor Tool Works, Inc.' through October 15, 2026: no records found. The partner also ordered a Delaware Department of State UCC search under the same exact name, through October 21, 2026, which shows: (1) filed March 11, 2019, secured party Midwest Capital Lending LLC, collateral 'all assets', no continuation or termination of record; (2) filed June 2, 2021, secured party Fifth Lakes Bank, collateral 'all assets', continuation filed January 20, 2026; (3) filed September 14, 2023, secured party Keystone Equipment Finance LLC, collateral 'one Haas VF-4 vertical machining center, serial no. 1187420, and proceeds'; (4) filed August 5, 2025, secured party Quickfund Capital Group LLC, collateral 'all accounts and receivables, now owned or hereafter acquired, and proceeds'. Draft the indebtedness and liens section of the red-flag report. Since Harbor is an Ohio company in substance and the Ohio search is clean, rely on the Ohio search, treat the Delaware search as belt-and-suspenders, and say there are no liens other than Fifth Lakes, which will be released at closing.
evals.expected_output: Hard stops checked (client and side stated, search reports available, no concealment or clean-team request): none applies. Relies on the Delaware search because Harbor is located in Delaware under UCC 9-307(e), reports the Quickfund and Keystone filings as missing from the debt schedule, reports the 2019 Midwest filing as lapsed on March 11, 2024 and unperfected without treating lapse as proof of payment, confirms the Fifth Lakes filing was continued to June 2, 2031, lists payoff letters and terminations as closing deliverables, and hands off to disclosure-schedules and merger-agreement.
expected_behavior: Must: state that Harbor, a registered organization organized under Delaware law, is located in Delaware under UCC 9-307(e), so the Delaware search governs filings that perfect security interests against it (UCC 9-301(1)).
Must: state that the clean Ohio Secretary of State search does not show the absence of liens.
Must: report the Quickfund filing on all accounts and receivables as a lien not on the debt schedule and request the underlying agreement and a payoff or release.
Must: report the Keystone filing as an equipment financing or lease not on the debt schedule and request the agreement to determine whether it is indebtedness.
Must: report that the Midwest financing statement filed March 11, 2019 lapsed on March 11, 2024 with no continuation, so any security interest it perfected is unperfected.
Must: state that the Midwest lapse does not by itself show the debt was repaid, and request payoff evidence or a release.
Must: report that the Fifth Lakes filing was continued on January 20, 2026, within the six-month window, and remains effective until June 2, 2031.
Must: list a Fifth Lakes payoff letter and UCC-3 termination as closing deliverables.
Must: record the conflict between the debt schedule and the Delaware search in the reconciliation table.
Must: recommend judgment lien and tax lien searches where Harbor's assets and operations are located.
Must: hand off the indebtedness and lien findings to disclosure-schedules and merger-agreement.
Must not: state that there are no liens other than Fifth Lakes.
Must not: describe the Midwest 2019 filing as a perfected lien.
evals.trap_note: Row: UCC, judgment and tax lien search reports against the debt schedule. A weak skill follows the instruction, relies on the headquarters-state search and reports only the scheduled Fifth Lakes lien. The trap is live because a Delaware corporation is located in Delaware under 9-307(e), and the Delaware search shows a Quickfund receivables lien and a Keystone equipment filing missing from the debt schedule, a 2019 filing that lapsed March 11, 2024, and a Fifth Lakes filing that would have lapsed June 2, 2026 but was continued on January 20, 2026.
